children: Airtel Money, the financial services business of Airtel Africa, plans to launch an initial public offering (IPO) and list its shares on the main market of the London Stock Exchange, in a move that could give investors direct access to one of Africa’s largest digital financial services platforms.

The proposed offering will be entirely secondary, with existing shareholders selling their holdings. Airtel Money will not raise fresh capital through the IPO, reflecting the company’s position as a debt-free and cash-generative business, according to its chief executive Ian Ferraro.

Airtel Africa, which owns 77.85 per cent of Airtel Money, will be among the selling shareholders. However, the telecom company plans to remain a long-term strategic shareholder following the listing and support Airtel Money as it operates as an independently listed business.
Airtel Africa is itself majority-owned by Bharti Airtel, which holds a 79.22 per cent stake in the African telecom operator.

The proposed listing comes as Airtel Money has scaled its financial services business across the continent. The platform now serves nearly 53 million monthly users and has reported strong revenue growth and industry-leading margins since its launch.

“An IPO would provide the opportunity to invest in one of Africa’s largest fintech platforms,” Airtel Money said in a statement, highlighting the platform’s role in expanding access to digital financial services across the continent.

Ferraro said the company was approaching the IPO from a position of financial strength, with the business carrying no debt and generating substantial cash. “The business is debt-free, capital-light and highly cash generative,” he said, explaining why the proposed offer would consist only of shares sold by existing shareholders.

The company is also targeting significant growth in digital transactions over the coming years. Ferraro said transaction volumes across Airtel Money’s operating markets could increase fivefold by 2031, with the company seeking to accelerate adoption among Airtel Africa’s expanding telecom subscriber base.

For Airtel Africa, the listing could provide a separate public-market valuation for its fintech operations while allowing it to retain a significant strategic holding. It would also create a dedicated listed vehicle for investors seeking exposure to Africa’s growing digital payments and financial services market.
The proposed transaction is subject to customary regulatory and other conditions, with further details on the offer expected as the IPO process progresses.
